rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one suitable measure, such as improved rearing methods, suitable feed, or protecting fish and their habitats from pollution or overfishing.

written.text: Differentiate between medicine and surgery
modelAnswer: Medicine treats disease mainly through drugs or other non-surgical methods.
Surgery treats disease through an operation or procedure on the body, such as repairing or removing tissue.
written.followUp: What is one main difference between treating a disease with medicine and treating it with surgery?

rubric.why: Medicine generally treats disease using drugs without an operation.
rubric.description: Describe medicine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that medicine uses drugs or other non-surgical treatment.

rubric.why: Surgery treats a condition by an operation, often involving work on body tissues.
rubric.description: Describe surgery and distinguish it from medicine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that surgery uses an operation or procedure, such as cutting, repairing or removing tissue.

written.text: The formulation of hypothesis is the most important step of biological method. Why ?
modelAnswer: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation that provides a basis and direction for investigating a biological problem.
Experiments test whether the hypothesis is correct.
written.followUp: Why is a hypothesis tested through experiments?

rubric.why: A hypothesis provides a basis or direction for investigating a biological problem.
rubric.description: Explains that a hypothesis directs the investigation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its role as the basis or direction of the investigation.

rubric.why: Experiments are planned to test the hypothesis.
rubric.description: States that experiments test the hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the hypothesis to experimental testing.

written.text: Write names of two words used for identification of deductions
modelAnswer: The two words used in deductions are “if” and “then”.
written.followUp: What are the two main parts of a deduction in the biological method?

rubric.why: The first word introduces the condition in a deduction.
rubric.description: Names “if”.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the first word.

rubric.why: The second word introduces the predicted result.
rubric.description: Names “then”.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the second word.

written.text: What is meant by bioinformatics ?
modelAnswer: Bioinformatics is the use of computers and information technology to store, manage and analyse biological data.
written.followUp: How does bioinformatics help in the study of biological information?

rubric.why: Bioinformatics applies computer-based tools to biological information.
rubric.description: Mentions the use of computers or information technology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the computer-based aspect.

rubric.why: The data being stored, managed or analysed are biological.
rubric.description: Identifies biological data as the subject of bioinformatics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to the handling or analysis of biological data.

written.text: Write down two drawbacks of absence of epidermal tissues in plants
modelAnswer: Without epidermal tissues, a plant would lose more water and may dry out.
It would also be less protected from mechanical injury and pathogens.
written.followUp: State two functions of the epidermis in plants.

rubric.why: Epidermal tissues help limit water loss from the plant.
rubric.description: States that the plant may lose excessive water or dry out.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this consequence of lacking epidermal tissue.

rubric.why: The epidermis protects the plant from injury and harmful organisms.
rubric.description: States that the plant is more vulnerable to injury or infection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second consequence of lacking epidermal tissue.

written.text: Write down two differences between Osmosis and diffusion
modelAnswer: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution.
Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration; it does not require a membrane.
written.followUp: Differentiate between osmosis and diffusion.

rubric.why: Osmosis specifically involves water moving through a selectively permeable membrane.
rubric.description: Gives the defining feature of osmosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying water movement through a selectively permeable membrane.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the net movement of particles down a concentration gradient and does not require a membrane.
rubric.description: Gives the defining feature of diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that particles move from higher to lower concentration, or that diffusion does not require a membrane.

written.text: Write properties of kingdom animalia
modelAnswer: Members of kingdom Animalia are multicellular eukaryotes.
They are heterotrophic and their cells do not have cell walls.
written.followUp: Write two characteristics of organisms belonging to kingdom Plantae.

rubric.why: Animals are multicellular eukaryotic organisms.
rubric.description: Gives a correct basic cellular characteristic of animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that animals are multicellular or eukaryotic.

rubric.why: Animals obtain food heterotrophically and their cells lack cell walls.
rubric.description: Gives a correct nutritional or cell-structure characteristic of animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that animals are heterotrophic or lack cell walls.

written.text: What do you know about Marcopolo sheep ?
modelAnswer: The Marco Polo sheep is a wild sheep found in the high mountains of Central Asia, especially the Pamir region.
It is well known for its very long, curved spiral horns.
written.followUp: Where is the Marco Polo sheep found, and what feature is it especially known for?

rubric.why: The Marco Polo sheep occurs in high mountain regions of Central Asia, including the Pamirs.
rubric.description: Gives an accurate region or mountain habitat for the sheep.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Central Asia, the Pamirs, or an appropriate northern mountain region.

rubric.why: Its long, curved, spiral horns are its distinctive feature.
rubric.description: Mentions its distinctive large or spiral horns.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this identifying feature.

written.text: What is the function of G0 phase in cell cycle ?
modelAnswer: In the G₀ phase, a cell leaves the active cell cycle and does not divide.
It may remain metabolically active while carrying out its normal functions.
written.followUp: What happens to a cell when it enters the G₀ phase?

rubric.why: In G₀, the cell leaves the active cell cycle.
rubric.description: Identifies G₀ as a phase in which the cell exits the active cell cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cell leaves or exits the cell cycle.

rubric.why: A cell in G₀ does not divide, although it can continue carrying out its normal functions.
rubric.description: States that the cell does not divide or continues its normal functions while in G₀.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the cell’s state or activity in G₀.

written.text: How cell plate is formed in cytokinesis ?
modelAnswer: Golgi vesicles gather and fuse at the equator of the dividing plant cell to form a cell plate.
The cell plate grows outward and develops into a new cell wall, separating the daughter cells.
written.followUp: Describe how the cell plate develops into a new cell wall during plant-cell cytokinesis.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the material and place where the cell plate begins to form.
rubric.description: Golgi vesicles gather at the equator and fuse.
rubric.how: Look for vesicles (or Golgi vesicles) accumulating or joining at the cell’s equator to form the plate; accept equivalent wording involving vesicles from the Golgi apparatus coming together there.

rubric.why: Award for describing how the plate grows and separates the daughter cells.
rubric.description: The cell plate grows outward and develops into a separating cell wall.
rubric.how: Look for growth of the plate towards the cell edges and/or its development into a new wall dividing the daughter cells.

written.text: How metaphase plate is formed in metaphase I of meiosis ?
modelAnswer: Homologous chromosome pairs (bivalents) arrange themselves along the equatorial plane, forming the metaphase plate.
Spindle fibres from opposite poles attach to the chromosomes at their centromeres.
written.followUp: How do homologous chromosomes orient at the equator during metaphase I?

rubric.why: This identifies the chromosome pairs and their position in metaphase I.
rubric.description: Homologous chromosome pairs (bivalents) line up at the equatorial plane.
rubric.how: Award for stating that homologous pairs or bivalents arrange at the equator.

rubric.why: This describes the spindle attachment that helps form the metaphase arrangement.
rubric.description: Spindle fibres from opposite poles attach to the chromosomes at their centromeres.
rubric.how: Award for stating that spindle fibres attach to the chromosomes at their centromeres.

written.text: Differentiate between light and dark reaction of photosynthesis
modelAnswer: The light reaction occurs in the thylakoids (grana), requires light, and produces ATP, NADPH and oxygen.
The dark reaction occurs in the stroma; it uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide into carbohydrates and does not directly require light.
written.followUp: Compare the light-dependent and light-independent stages of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Award for a correct feature of the light reaction.
rubric.description: The light reaction takes place in the thylakoids (grana) and requires light.
rubric.how: Look for the light requirement and/or its location in the thylakoids or grana.

rubric.why: Award for a correct contrast describing the dark reaction.
rubric.description: The dark reaction occurs in the stroma and uses carbon dioxide and products of the light reaction to make carbohydrates.
rubric.how: Look for its location in the stroma and/or the use of carbon dioxide with ATP and NADPH to form carbohydrates; accept that it does not directly require light.

written.text: Why enzymes are helpful in biological reactions ?
modelAnswer: Enzymes lower the activation energy required for biological reactions.
This makes the reactions occur faster, while the enzymes remain unchanged and can be reused.
written.followUp: Explain how enzymes increase the rate of biochemical reactions.

rubric.why: Award for stating the mechanism by which enzymes speed reactions.
rubric.description: Enzymes lower the activation energy of reactions.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that enzymes reduce or lower the activation energy needed for a reaction.

rubric.why: Award for explaining the effect or reusable nature of enzymes.
rubric.description: This makes reactions faster; enzymes are not used up in the reactions.
rubric.how: Look for a statement that reactions proceed faster and/or that enzymes remain unchanged and can be reused.

written.text: What are the uses of enzymes in food industry ?
modelAnswer: Amylase is used in bread making.
Rennin (rennet) is used in cheese making.
written.followUp: Give two examples of enzymes used in food processing and state what each is used for.

rubric.why: Award for one correct enzyme and its food-industry use.
rubric.description: One valid enzyme application is identified.
rubric.how: Look for a correct enzyme-use pair, such as amylase in bread making, rennin in cheese making, protease for meat tenderising, or pectinase in juice processing.

rubric.why: Award for a second valid enzyme application.
rubric.description: A second valid enzyme application is identified.
rubric.how: Look for another correct enzyme-use pair; it must be different from the example credited for the first mark.

written.text: What is myocardial infarction ?
modelAnswer: Myocardial infarction, or a heart attack, occurs when a coronary artery is blocked.
The affected heart muscle receives too little oxygen, causing some of its tissue to become damaged or die.
written.followUp: What causes a heart attack, and why does it damage heart muscle?

rubric.why: Award for identifying the blocked blood supply that causes the condition.
rubric.description: A coronary artery becomes blocked or obstructed.
rubric.how: Look for blockage or obstruction of a coronary artery, or an equivalent statement that blood supply to the heart muscle is cut off.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the resulting damage to the heart muscle.
rubric.description: The affected heart muscle is deprived of oxygen and is damaged or dies.
rubric.how: Look for oxygen deprivation and damage or death of heart muscle; accepting “heart attack” as a synonym requires the cause or effect to be stated as well for this mark.

written.text: Give two points about the importance of transpiration
modelAnswer: Transpiration helps in the upward transport of water and mineral salts from the roots to the leaves (ascent of sap).
It also cools the plant and helps maintain cell turgidity.
written.followUp: State two ways in which transpiration is important to a plant.

rubric.why: Award for a role in moving water or minerals through the plant.
rubric.description: Transpiration helps move water and mineral salts from roots towards the leaves.
rubric.how: Look for ascent of sap or transport of water and minerals from roots to leaves.

rubric.why: Award for another valid importance of transpiration.
rubric.description: Transpiration cools the plant and/or helps maintain cell turgidity.
rubric.how: Look for cooling or maintenance of turgidity; do not award this mark for merely repeating water or mineral transport.

written.text: How transpiration pull is created ?
modelAnswer: Water evaporates from the moist mesophyll cells of leaves and diffuses out through the stomata.
This water loss creates tension (suction) in the xylem, pulling the continuous column of water upward from the roots.
written.followUp: Explain how cohesion between water molecules helps maintain transpiration pull.

rubric.why: Identifies water loss from the leaf as the event that initiates transpiration pull.
rubric.description: Water evaporates from the moist mesophyll cells and diffuses out through the stomata.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing evaporation or water loss from leaf tissues.

rubric.why: Explains that water loss creates a pulling force transmitted through the xylem.
rubric.description: Water loss creates tension or suction in the xylem, pulling the continuous water column upward from the roots.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking tension or suction in the xylem to upward movement of water.

written.text: How can you distinguish between ingestion and digestion ?
modelAnswer: Ingestion is the taking of food into the body through the mouth.
Digestion is the mechanical and chemical breakdown of complex food into simple, soluble substances that can be absorbed.
written.followUp: Distinguish between absorption and assimilation in nutrition.

rubric.why: States that ingestion is the intake of food.
rubric.description: Ingestion is taking food into the body through the mouth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct meaning of ingestion.

rubric.why: States that digestion breaks food down into simpler substances.
rubric.description: Digestion is the mechanical and chemical breakdown of complex food into simple, soluble substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct meaning of digestion.

written.text: What are the sources of carbohydrates ?
modelAnswer: Plants make carbohydrates by photosynthesis.
Common dietary sources include cereals such as rice, wheat and maize, as well as potatoes, sugarcane and fruits.
written.followUp: Name three foods that are rich sources of carbohydrates.

rubric.why: Identifies plants as the main source of carbohydrates.
rubric.description: Plants make carbohydrates by photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying plants or photosynthesis as the source.

rubric.why: Gives examples of foods that supply carbohydrates.
rubric.description: Examples include cereals and foods such as rice, wheat, maize, potatoes, sugarcane and fruits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving suitable examples of carbohydrate sources.

written.text: What are fertilizers ? Name their types
modelAnswer: Fertilizers are substances added to soil to supply nutrients and improve its fertility for plant growth.
The two main types are organic fertilizers and inorganic (chemical) fertilizers.
written.followUp: What is manure? Give two examples of organic fertilizers.

rubric.why: Defines fertilizers by their use in supplying nutrients or improving soil fertility.
rubric.description: Fertilizers are substances added to soil to supply nutrients and improve its fertility for plant growth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition or purpose.

rubric.why: Names the two main types of fertilizers.
rubric.description: The types are organic fertilizers and inorganic (chemical) fertilizers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both types.

written.text: How transport of water takes place in plants ?
modelAnswer: Root hairs absorb water from the soil, mainly by osmosis.
Water passes across the root cortex and enters the xylem.
Xylem vessels carry water and dissolved mineral salts upward through the stem to the leaves.
Transpiration from leaves creates a pull that draws the water column upward.
Cohesion between water molecules and adhesion to xylem walls help keep the column continuous; root pressure may also assist.
written.followUp: Describe how minerals dissolved in soil water reach the leaves of a plant.

rubric.why: Describes the entry of water into the plant.
rubric.description: Root hairs absorb water from the soil, mainly by osmosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming root hairs and water absorption (osmosis where specified).

rubric.why: Shows the route water takes through the root to reach the conducting tissue.
rubric.description: Water passes through the root cortex and enters the xylem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing passage through the root to the xylem.

rubric.why: Identifies the tissue that carries water upward through the plant.
rubric.description: Water and dissolved minerals move upward through xylem vessels in the stem to the leaves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying xylem as the transport tissue.

rubric.why: Explains the forces responsible for the upward movement of water.
rubric.description: Transpiration pull is the main force; cohesion between water molecules and adhesion to xylem walls help maintain the water column. Root pressure may also assist.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for explaining transpiration pull and at least one supporting force or mechanism.

written.text: Do you think that the food is oxidized without oxygen ? How and by which methods ?
modelAnswer: Yes. Food can be broken down in the absence of oxygen by anaerobic respiration, an incomplete breakdown of glucose.
In yeast, anaerobic respiration is called fermentation and produces ethanol, carbon dioxide and a small amount of energy.
In muscle cells, glucose may be broken down without oxygen to form lactic acid and release a small amount of energy.
written.followUp: Compare aerobic respiration with anaerobic respiration, giving the products of each.

rubric.why: Answers that food can be broken down without oxygen and names the process.
rubric.description: Yes. Food can be broken down in the absence of oxygen by anaerobic respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear yes and identification of anaerobic respiration.

rubric.why: Identifies the conditions or nature of the process.
rubric.description: Anaerobic respiration is an incomplete breakdown of glucose in the absence of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the absence of oxygen or incomplete breakdown.

rubric.why: Names a common organism or method associated with anaerobic breakdown.
rubric.description: In yeast, this process is called fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying yeast or fermentation.

rubric.why: Gives the products of anaerobic breakdown in yeast or muscle cells.
rubric.description: Yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide; muscle cells can produce lactic acid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct product set.

rubric.why: Notes that anaerobic respiration releases energy.
rubric.description: The process releases a small amount of energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that energy is released.

written.text: Write the brief note on compound tissues of plants
modelAnswer: Compound tissues are made of different types of cells that work together to perform a common function.
Xylem transports water and mineral salts from the roots to other parts of the plant; it consists of vessels, tracheids, fibres and parenchyma.
Phloem transports prepared food from leaves to other parts of the plant; it consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, fibres and parenchyma.
written.followUp: Name the conducting tissues in plants, give their main components, and state the function of each.

rubric.why: Defines a compound tissue as different cell types working together.
rubric.description: A compound tissue consists of different types of cells that work together to perform a common function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition of compound tissue.

rubric.why: Identifies xylem and its transport function.
rubric.description: Xylem transports water and mineral salts from the roots to other parts of the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming xylem and stating that it transports water and mineral salts.

rubric.why: Identifies phloem and its transport function.
rubric.description: Phloem transports prepared food from leaves to other parts of the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming phloem and stating that it transports food.

rubric.why: Gives the main cell components of the compound conducting tissues.
rubric.description: Xylem includes vessels, tracheids, fibres and parenchyma; phloem includes sieve tubes, companion cells, fibres and parenchyma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least two suitable components of xylem or phloem.

written.text: How stomach play role in the process of digestion
modelAnswer: The muscular walls of the stomach churn and mix food with gastric juice.
Hydrochloric acid in gastric juice makes the contents acidic and helps kill germs.
Pepsin digests proteins into smaller peptides.
Mucus protects the lining of the stomach from acid and digestive enzymes.
The partly digested, semi-liquid food is called chyme and passes into the small intestine.
written.followUp: Describe the roles of the small intestine in digestion.

rubric.why: The stomach’s muscular walls churn food and mix it with gastric juice.
rubric.description: Churning and mixing
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the stomach churns or mixes food with gastric juice.

rubric.why: Hydrochloric acid makes the stomach contents acidic and helps kill germs.
rubric.description: Role of hydrochloric acid
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct role of hydrochloric acid in the stomach.

rubric.why: Pepsin digests proteins into smaller peptides.
rubric.description: Role of pepsin
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pepsin digests proteins into peptides.

rubric.why: Mucus protects the stomach lining from acid and digestive enzymes.
rubric.description: Protective role of mucus
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mucus protects the stomach lining or wall.

rubric.why: The partly digested food, called chyme, passes from the stomach into the small intestine.
rubric.description: Formation and passage of chyme
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chyme and stating that it passes into the small intestine.

written.text: Write two benefits of horticulture.
modelAnswer: Horticulture provides fruits, vegetables and flowers for food and other uses.
It creates income and employment, and ornamental plants beautify the surroundings.
written.followUp: Write two benefits of agriculture.

rubric.why: Horticulture provides useful produce, including fruits and vegetables.
rubric.description: Provides food and useful produce
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a food or useful plant product provided by horticulture.

rubric.why: Horticulture can provide economic benefits or beautify surroundings through ornamental plants.
rubric.description: Economic or aesthetic benefit
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one distinct benefit, such as income, employment or beautification.

written.text: How bioeconomics is useful in the field of biology?
modelAnswer: Bioeconomics deals with the economic use of biological knowledge, resources and products.
It helps people make effective use of biological resources and gain economic benefits from them.
written.followUp: What is biotechnology, and how is it useful to people?

rubric.why: Bioeconomics concerns the economic use of biological knowledge, resources and products.
rubric.description: Meaning of bioeconomics
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking biology or biological resources/products with economic use.

rubric.why: Bioeconomics helps people use biological resources effectively and gain economic benefits.
rubric.description: Use of bioeconomics
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it supports effective use of biological resources or economic benefit from them.

written.text: Write any two professions names to which only bio students can adopt.
modelAnswer: Medical doctor
Veterinary doctor
written.followUp: Name two professions in which the study of biology is important.

rubric.why: A medical profession is one career requiring biology.
rubric.description: One biology-related profession
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid profession requiring biology.

rubric.why: A second distinct biology-related profession is required.
rubric.description: A second biology-related profession
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different valid profession requiring biology.

written.text: How can you differentiate between controlled group and experimental group?
modelAnswer: The controlled group is kept under normal conditions and does not receive the factor being tested.
The experimental group receives the factor being tested so that its effect can be observed.
written.followUp: In an experiment, what is the purpose of keeping a control group?

rubric.why: The control group does not receive the factor being tested and is kept under normal conditions.
rubric.description: Control group
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the control group.

rubric.why: The experimental group receives the factor whose effect is being investigated.
rubric.description: Experimental group
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the experimental group.

written.text: Which type of observations are accurate and why?
modelAnswer: Quantitative observations are more accurate than qualitative observations.
They are measured and expressed in numbers, so they are less dependent on personal judgement.
written.followUp: Differentiate between qualitative and quantitative observations.

rubric.why: Quantitative observations are measured or expressed numerically.
rubric.description: Identifies quantitative observations
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying quantitative observations as the more accurate type.

rubric.why: Measurements and numerical results are less dependent on personal judgement.
rubric.description: Explains why they are accurate
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that quantitative observations are measurable, numerical or more objective.

written.text: Differentiate between biological method and biological problem.
modelAnswer: A biological problem is a question or issue about living organisms that needs to be investigated.
The biological method is the systematic procedure used to investigate and solve a biological problem.
written.followUp: List the main steps of the biological method.

rubric.why: A biological problem is the question or issue that needs to be investigated.
rubric.description: Biological problem
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a biological problem as a question or issue about living organisms.

rubric.why: The biological method is the systematic procedure used to investigate and solve such a problem.
rubric.description: Biological method
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the biological method as the steps or procedure used to solve a biological problem.

written.text: What do you know about DeDuve?
modelAnswer: Christian de Duve was a Belgian scientist who discovered lysosomes.
He received the Nobel Prize in 1974 for discoveries concerning the structural and functional organization of the cell.
written.followUp: Name the cell organelle discovered by Christian de Duve and state one function of it.

rubric.why: Christian de Duve is best known in this context for discovering lysosomes.
rubric.description: Discovery
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the discovery of lysosomes.

rubric.why: His recognition with the 1974 Nobel Prize is a relevant fact about him.
rubric.description: Recognition
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that he received the Nobel Prize in 1974.

written.text: Do you know about hypertonic and hypotonic solutions?
modelAnswer: A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the cell, so water moves out of the cell by osmosis.
A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell, so water moves into the cell by osmosis.
written.followUp: How do hypertonic and hypotonic solutions affect the size of an animal cell?

rubric.why: Tests the definition of a hypertonic solution and the resulting direction of osmosis.
rubric.description: States that a hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the cell, so water moves out of the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the higher external solute concentration relative to the cell and the outward movement of water.

rubric.why: Tests the definition of a hypotonic solution and the resulting direction of osmosis.
rubric.description: States that a hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell, so water moves into the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the lower external solute concentration relative to the cell and the inward movement of water.

written.text: Write names of any four extinct animals.
modelAnswer: Dodo
Woolly mammoth
Passenger pigeon
Dinosaurs
written.followUp: Name four animals that are endangered or threatened with extinction.

rubric.why: Checks that an extinct animal is correctly named.
rubric.description: Names two extinct animals.
rubric.how: Award ½ mark for each correct extinct animal, up to 1 mark for two. Accept any valid examples, including dinosaurs, dodo, mammoth, passenger pigeon or Tasmanian tiger.

rubric.why: Checks that further examples are correctly named.
rubric.description: Names two more extinct animals.
rubric.how: Award ½ mark for each additional correct extinct animal, up to 1 mark for two. Accept any valid examples; do not award twice for the same animal.

written.text: Differentiate between Monera and Protista.
modelAnswer: Monera are prokaryotic organisms; their cells lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus.
Protista are eukaryotic organisms; their cells have a true, membrane-bound nucleus.
written.followUp: State one difference between the cells of Monera and Protista.

rubric.why: Tests a defining cell feature of kingdom Monera.
rubric.description: States that Monera are prokaryotic and lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Monera as prokaryotic or stating that its cells lack a true nucleus or nuclear membrane.

rubric.why: Tests the contrasting cell feature of kingdom Protista.
rubric.description: States that Protista are eukaryotic and have a true, membrane-bound nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Protista as eukaryotic or stating that its cells have a true nucleus or nuclear membrane.

written.text: What is the importance of crossing over in meiosis?
modelAnswer: During prophase I of meiosis, non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes exchange corresponding segments of genetic material.
This produces new combinations of genes and increases genetic variation.
written.followUp: During which stage of meiosis does crossing over occur, and what is exchanged?

accept: exchange corresponding segments of genetic material
rubric.why: Tests what crossing over involves and which chromosomes participate.
rubric.description: States that corresponding segments of genetic material are exchanged between homologous chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the exchange of genetic material segments between homologous chromosomes.

rubric.why: Tests the biological importance of crossing over.
rubric.description: Explains that crossing over creates new gene combinations and increases genetic variation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that crossing over produces new gene combinations or increases genetic variation.

written.text: What is synapsis? Where it occurs?
modelAnswer: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes.
It occurs during prophase I of meiosis, specifically in the zygotene stage.
written.followUp: What is a bivalent, and during which stage of meiosis is it formed?

rubric.why: Tests the meaning of synapsis.
rubric.description: Defines synapsis as the pairing of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the pairing or coming together of homologous chromosomes.

rubric.why: Tests where synapsis occurs in meiosis.
rubric.description: Locates synapsis in prophase I, specifically the zygotene stage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating prophase I or, more specifically, zygotene.

written.text: Define meiosis. Who discovered it?
modelAnswer: Meiosis is a reduction division in which one diploid cell produces four haploid daughter cells, each with half the chromosome number of the parent cell.
Meiosis was discovered by Oscar Hertwig in 1876.
written.followUp: How many daughter cells are produced by meiosis, and how does their chromosome number compare with the parent cell?

rubric.why: Tests the definition and outcome of meiosis.
rubric.description: Defines meiosis as a reduction division that produces haploid cells with half the chromosome number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing meiosis as reduction division or stating that it produces four haploid daughter cells with half the parent cell's chromosome number.

rubric.why: Tests recall of the scientist associated with the discovery of meiosis.
rubric.description: Names Oscar Hertwig as the discoverer of meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Oscar Hertwig.

written.text: Why oxidation reduction reaction is called redox reaction?
modelAnswer: Oxidation is the loss of electrons, while reduction is the gain of electrons.
In a reaction, oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously; therefore, it is called a redox reaction.
written.followUp: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer.

rubric.why: Tests the electron-transfer definition of oxidation.
rubric.description: States that oxidation is the loss of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining oxidation as loss of electrons.

rubric.why: Tests the paired nature of oxidation and reduction in a redox reaction.
rubric.description: Explains that reduction is gain of electrons and that oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the two processes occur together; accept the electron-transfer definition of reduction when it is correctly paired with oxidation.

written.text: What do you know about the accessory pigments?
modelAnswer: Accessory pigments include chlorophyll b and carotenoids, such as carotenes and xanthophylls.
They absorb light wavelengths that chlorophyll a absorbs poorly and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a for photosynthesis.
written.followUp: Name two accessory pigments and state how they help in photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Award for identifying accessory pigments.
rubric.description: Names accessory pigments such as chlorophyll b and carotenoids.
rubric.how: Accept either a correct pigment name or group of pigments.

rubric.why: Accessory pigments broaden the range of light absorbed for photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Explains that accessory pigments absorb light and transfer its energy to chlorophyll a.
rubric.how: Require the idea of light absorption and energy transfer to chlorophyll a.

written.text: Differentiate between insoluble and soluble dietary fibers.
modelAnswer: Soluble dietary fibre dissolves in water and can form a gel.
Insoluble dietary fibre does not dissolve in water; it adds bulk to faeces and helps bowel movement.
written.followUp: State one difference between soluble and insoluble dietary fibre.

rubric.why: Solubility in water is the defining difference for soluble fibre.
rubric.description: States that soluble dietary fibre dissolves in water.
rubric.how: Require an explicit statement that soluble fibre dissolves in water.

rubric.why: Insoluble fibre is distinguished by not dissolving in water.
rubric.description: States that insoluble dietary fibre does not dissolve in water.
rubric.how: Require an explicit statement that insoluble fibre does not dissolve in water.

written.text: What is heart beat and pulse rate?
modelAnswer: A heartbeat is one rhythmic cycle of contraction and relaxation of the heart.
Pulse rate is the number of pulses in the arteries per minute, produced by the heartbeats.
written.followUp: How is pulse rate related to the heartbeat?

rubric.why: A heartbeat is one cycle of the heart’s rhythmic activity.
rubric.description: Defines a heartbeat as the heart’s rhythmic cycle of contraction and relaxation.
rubric.how: Require the heart’s rhythmic action and both contraction and relaxation.

rubric.why: Pulse rate is the number of arterial pulses counted per minute.
rubric.description: Defines pulse rate as the number of pulses in the arteries per minute.
rubric.how: Require pulses counted per minute and identify their arterial location.

written.text: How would you explain the structure and functions of compound tissues?
modelAnswer: Compound tissues consist of different types of cells that work together to perform a common function.
Xylem is made up of vessels, tracheids, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.
Xylem carries water and mineral salts from the roots towards the leaves and also provides support.
Phloem is made up of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres.
Phloem transports (translocates) food made in the leaves to other parts of the plant.
written.followUp: Name the cell types in xylem and phloem, and state the function of each tissue.

rubric.why: Compound tissues consist of different kinds of cells working together.
rubric.description: Defines compound tissues as tissues made of different cell types that work together.
rubric.how: Require both multiple cell types and their cooperation in a function.

rubric.why: Vessels, tracheids, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres are the principal components of xylem.
rubric.description: Names the four main components of xylem.
rubric.how: Require all four components; accept either spelling of fibres.

rubric.why: Xylem transports water and mineral salts from roots towards leaves.
rubric.description: States that xylem carries water and minerals from the roots towards the leaves.
rubric.how: Require the materials transported and the direction or source and destination.

rubric.why: Sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres are the principal components of phloem.
rubric.description: Names the four main components of phloem.
rubric.how: Require all four components; accept either spelling of fibres.

rubric.why: Phloem transports food made in leaves to other parts of the plant.
rubric.description: States that phloem transports or translocates food from leaves to other parts of the plant.
rubric.how: Require food transport and identify leaves as its source or other plant parts as its destination.

written.text: What do you think about liver? Is it a vital organ which helps in digestion? How? Explain.
modelAnswer: The liver is a vital organ and the largest gland of the body; it performs essential functions, including processing nutrients and detoxifying harmful substances.
It produces bile, which is stored in the gall bladder and released into the small intestine.
Bile salts emulsify large fat globules into tiny droplets; bile is not an enzyme.
This increases the surface area for lipase to digest fats, and the alkaline bile also helps neutralise acidic chyme from the stomach.
written.followUp: Describe how bile helps in the digestion of fats and name one other important function of the liver.

rubric.why: The question asks whether the liver is a vital organ.
rubric.description: Identifies the liver as a vital or essential organ.
rubric.how: Require an explicit statement that the liver is vital or essential.

rubric.why: Bile is the liver’s main digestive secretion.
rubric.description: States that the liver produces or secretes bile.
rubric.how: Require the liver to be identified as the source of bile.

rubric.why: Bile salts emulsify large fat globules into smaller droplets.
rubric.description: Explains that bile emulsifies fats into small droplets.
rubric.how: Require emulsification or the breaking up of fat globules into smaller droplets.

rubric.why: Emulsification increases the surface area for lipase, and bile also helps neutralise acidic chyme.
rubric.description: Explains a digestive benefit of bile, such as aiding lipase action or neutralising acidic chyme.
rubric.how: Require one correct explanation of how bile assists digestion.

written.text: How cells are organized? Give types of cellular organization.
modelAnswer: Organisms show three types of cellular organization: unicellular, colonial and multicellular.
A unicellular organism consists of one cell; a colonial organism has cells living together in a group; a multicellular organism consists of many specialized cells.
written.followUp: Name the three types of cellular organization and give one example of each.

rubric.why: Identifies the three types of cellular organization.
rubric.description: Names unicellular, colonial and multicellular organization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming all three types.

rubric.why: Shows how organisms are organized in each type.
rubric.description: Describes unicellular organisms as one cell, colonial organisms as cells living together in a group, and multicellular organisms as many cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for accurately describing all three types.

written.text: Write four unicellular organisms.
modelAnswer: Amoeba
Paramecium
Euglena
Bacteria
written.followUp: Write the names of four multicellular organisms.

rubric.why: Two correct examples establish knowledge of unicellular organisms.
rubric.description: Gives two correct unicellular organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct examples.

rubric.why: Completes the required set of four examples.
rubric.description: Gives two additional correct unicellular organisms, making four in total.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for four correct examples in total.

written.text: Differentiate between experimental and controlled group.
modelAnswer: The experimental group is exposed to the variable or treatment being tested.
The controlled group is not given that treatment and serves as a basis for comparison.
written.followUp: In an experiment testing the effect of light on plant growth, identify the experimental and controlled groups.

rubric.why: Identifies the group receiving the tested condition.
rubric.description: The experimental group receives the treatment or is exposed to the variable being tested.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the experimental-group distinction.

rubric.why: Identifies the comparison group that does not receive the tested treatment.
rubric.description: The controlled group is kept without the experimental treatment and is used for comparison.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the controlled-group distinction.

written.text: How biological problem is identified?
modelAnswer: A biological problem is identified by observing a biological phenomenon or condition that needs an explanation.
The observation is used to state a clear, specific problem or question for investigation.
written.followUp: What is a biological observation, and how can it help identify a biological problem?

rubric.why: Identifying a biological problem begins with noticing or observing a biological phenomenon.
rubric.description: States that the problem is recognized through observation of an event, condition or phenomenon.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking identification to observation.

rubric.why: The observation should lead to a definite problem to investigate.
rubric.description: Explains that the observed issue is stated clearly as a biological problem or question.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the problem clearly.

written.text: How the types of solution can be explained according to tonicity?
modelAnswer: A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration and a higher water concentration than the cell; water moves into the cell.
A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration and a lower water concentration than the cell; water moves out of the cell.
An isotonic solution has the same solute concentration as the cell, so there is no net movement of water.
written.followUp: What happens to an animal cell placed in a hypotonic solution?

rubric.why: Defines hypotonicity in relation to the cell or another solution.
rubric.description: A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration (and higher water concentration) than the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relative concentration.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the opposite concentration condition.
rubric.description: A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration (and lower water concentration) than the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relative concentration.

written.text: Explain nucleoid.
modelAnswer: The nucleoid is the region of a prokaryotic cell that contains its genetic material (DNA).
It is not surrounded by a nuclear membrane.
written.followUp: What is the nucleoid, and in which cells is it found?

rubric.why: Locates the nucleoid in cells without a true nucleus.
rubric.description: States that the nucleoid is found in prokaryotic cells, such as bacteria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its location.

rubric.why: Describes the nucleoid's contents and lack of a surrounding membrane.
rubric.description: Explains that it is the region containing the cell's DNA and is not enclosed by a membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an accurate description.

written.text: How taxonomy differs from systematics?
modelAnswer: Taxonomy deals with the identification, naming (nomenclature) and classification of organisms.
Systematics is broader: it studies the diversity of organisms and their relationships, including evolutionary relationships.
written.followUp: What does systematics study besides the naming and classification of organisms?

rubric.why: Taxonomy is concerned with identifying, naming and classifying organisms.
rubric.description: Defines taxonomy through identification, nomenclature and classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the role of taxonomy.

rubric.why: Systematics includes the study of diversity and relationships among organisms.
rubric.description: Distinguishes systematics by its study of organismal diversity and relationships, including evolutionary relationships.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the distinguishing feature of systematics.

written.text: Write two main characters of kingdom fungi.
modelAnswer: Fungi are eukaryotic organisms.
They lack chlorophyll and have cell walls made of chitin.
written.followUp: Write two characteristics of kingdom Plantae.

rubric.why: One valid characteristic of fungi is required.
rubric.description: States one characteristic of fungi.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one accurate characteristic, such as being eukaryotic, lacking chlorophyll, having chitin cell walls, or being heterotrophic.

rubric.why: A second valid characteristic is required.
rubric.description: States a second characteristic of fungi.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different accurate characteristic.

written.text: How cytokinesis occur in plants?
modelAnswer: Golgi vesicles gather at the equator of the plant cell and fuse to form a cell plate.
The cell plate grows outward until it joins the cell wall, separating the cytoplasm into two daughter cells.
written.followUp: Explain how cytokinesis occurs in animal cells.

rubric.why: Plant cytokinesis begins with the formation of a cell plate from vesicles.
rubric.description: Describes formation of the cell plate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Golgi vesicles gather and fuse at the equator to form a cell plate.

rubric.why: The cell plate grows across the cell and separates the cytoplasm into two daughter cells.
rubric.description: Explains how the cell plate completes division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the plate grows outward to join the cell wall and divides the cytoplasm.

written.text: Define tumors. How they formed?
modelAnswer: A tumor is an abnormal mass of cells.
It forms when cells divide uncontrollably, often because mutations disrupt the normal control of the cell cycle.
written.followUp: What is cancer, and how can it develop?

rubric.why: A tumor is an abnormal mass or growth of cells.
rubric.description: Defines a tumor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a tumor as an abnormal mass or growth of cells.

rubric.why: Tumors develop when cell division becomes uncontrolled, often following changes in cell-cycle control.
rubric.description: Explains tumor formation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking tumor formation to uncontrolled cell division or growth, or to mutations disrupting cell-cycle control.

written.text: How alcoholic fermentation differs from lactic acid fermentation?
modelAnswer: Alcoholic fermentation, commonly carried out by yeast, produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
Lactic acid fermentation, which occurs in some bacteria and in muscle cells, produces lactic acid.
written.followUp: Compare aerobic respiration with anaerobic respiration in yeast.

rubric.why: Alcoholic fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide, commonly in yeast.
rubric.description: States the products of alcoholic fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying ethanol and carbon dioxide as its products.

rubric.why: Lactic acid fermentation produces lactic acid rather than ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.description: States the product of lactic acid fermentation and distinguishes it from alcoholic fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying lactic acid as the product; accept mention of muscle cells or bacteria as the site.

written.text: Write the role of light intensity on the process of photosynthesis.
modelAnswer: As light intensity increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases while light is a limiting factor.
At high light intensity, the rate levels off because another factor becomes limiting.
written.followUp: How does carbon dioxide concentration affect the rate of photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Increasing light intensity generally increases the rate of photosynthesis when light is limiting.
rubric.description: States the effect of increasing light intensity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking greater light intensity with a higher photosynthesis rate, or low light with a low rate.

rubric.why: The rate eventually levels off when another factor becomes limiting or the light response reaches saturation.
rubric.description: Describes the limit to the effect of light intensity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate stops increasing at high intensity because another factor becomes limiting or the rate reaches saturation.

written.text: Differentiate between prosthetic group and metabolic pathway.
modelAnswer: A prosthetic group is a non-protein component that is tightly bound to an enzyme and is needed for its activity.
A metabolic pathway is a series of linked, enzyme-catalysed reactions that converts a starting substance into products.
written.followUp: Differentiate between a cofactor and a coenzyme.

rubric.why: A prosthetic group is a non-protein component tightly associated with an enzyme and needed for its activity.
rubric.description: Defines a prosthetic group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a non-protein component tightly bound to an enzyme.

rubric.why: A metabolic pathway is a sequence of enzyme-catalysed reactions that converts starting substances into products.
rubric.description: Defines a metabolic pathway.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a metabolic pathway as a series of linked chemical reactions, usually catalysed by enzymes.

written.text: What is meant by assimilation?
modelAnswer: Assimilation is the process by which absorbed nutrients are incorporated into body cells and used to build tissues or become part of the body's living material.
written.followUp: Define digestion and explain how it differs from absorption.

rubric.why: Assimilation is the use or incorporation of absorbed nutrients into the body's cells and tissues.
rubric.description: Defines assimilation.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for explaining that absorbed food or nutrients are incorporated into body material, used to build tissues, or used by cells.

written.text: Define nutrition. Also differentiate between macronutrients and micronutrients.
modelAnswer: Nutrition is the process by which organisms obtain and use food or nutrients for life and growth.
Macronutrients, such as carbohydrates, proteins and fats, are needed in large amounts; micronutrients, such as vitamins and minerals, are needed in small amounts.
written.followUp: Differentiate between carbohydrates and vitamins as nutrients.

rubric.why: Nutrition is the process of obtaining and using food or nutrients for life and growth.
rubric.description: Defines nutrition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining nutrition as obtaining and using nutrients or food by an organism.

rubric.why: Macronutrients are needed in relatively large amounts, whereas micronutrients are needed in small amounts.
rubric.description: Distinguishes macronutrients from micronutrients.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correct relative amounts required; examples such as carbohydrates, proteins and fats, or vitamins and minerals, may support the distinction.

written.text: Write any two functions of liver.
modelAnswer: The liver produces bile, which helps in the digestion of fats.
The liver also detoxifies harmful substances in the blood.
written.followUp: Write any two functions of the kidneys.

rubric.why: Bile production is a major function of the liver.
rubric.description: Names bile production as one liver function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver produces bile.

rubric.why: Any one additional correct function is sufficient.
rubric.description: Names another liver function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any correct function other than bile production.

written.text: Define the term systole and diastole.
modelAnswer: Systole is the phase in which the heart muscle contracts and pumps blood out of the heart.
Diastole is the phase in which the heart muscle relaxes and its chambers fill with blood.
written.followUp: Define the terms heartbeat and pulse.

rubric.why: Systole is the contraction phase of the heart.
rubric.description: Defines systole.

rubric.why: Diastole is the relaxation phase of the heart.
rubric.description: Defines diastole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying heart relaxation, with or without mentioning filling with blood.

written.text: What do you mean by agglutination and angioplasty?
modelAnswer: Agglutination is the clumping together of red blood cells when incompatible blood groups react due to antigens and antibodies.
Angioplasty is a procedure used to widen a narrowed or blocked artery, usually by inserting and inflating a balloon catheter.
written.followUp: What is a blood transfusion, and why is blood-group matching necessary?

rubric.why: Agglutination is the clumping of red blood cells following an antigen–antibody reaction.
rubric.description: Defines agglutination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that red blood cells clump together, usually due to an antigen–antibody reaction.

rubric.why: Angioplasty opens or widens a narrowed or blocked blood vessel.
rubric.description: Defines angioplasty.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that angioplasty widens or opens a narrowed or blocked artery, typically using a balloon catheter.

written.text: Define the blood group system and write names of four blood groups.
modelAnswer: The blood group system classifies blood according to the presence or absence of specific antigens on red blood cells.
The four blood groups are A, B, AB and O.
written.followUp: Name the four ABO blood groups and state what determines a person's ABO group.

rubric.why: Blood groups are classified according to the antigens present or absent on red blood cells.
rubric.description: Defines the blood group system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as a classification of blood based on red-cell antigens.

rubric.why: These are the four groups in the ABO system.
rubric.description: Names the four blood groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for listing A, B, AB and O.

written.text: Explain the relationship of biology to other sciences.
modelAnswer: Biology is linked with physics in biophysics, which applies physical principles to living organisms and their processes.
Biology is linked with chemistry in biochemistry, which studies the chemical substances and reactions occurring in organisms.
Biomathematics uses mathematical and statistical methods to analyse biological data.
Biogeography studies the geographical distribution of organisms.
Bioeconomics applies economic principles to biological resources and their use.
written.followUp: Explain how biology is related to chemistry and mathematics.

rubric.why: Biophysics applies principles of physics to biological structures and processes.
rubric.description: Explains the relationship between biology and physics.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for naming biophysics and explaining that it applies physics to living organisms or biological processes.

rubric.why: Biochemistry studies the chemical substances and reactions of living organisms.
rubric.description: Explains the relationship between biology and chemistry.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for naming biochemistry and explaining its study of chemicals or chemical reactions in organisms.

rubric.why: Other sciences also provide methods for studying biological data and the distribution or use of organisms.
rubric.description: Gives another valid biological connection with a science.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as biomathematics, biogeography or bioeconomics, with an appropriate explanation where needed.

written.text: Write a comprehensive note on white blood cells.
modelAnswer: White blood cells, or leucocytes, are colourless blood cells that have a nucleus.
They are classified into granulocytes and agranulocytes; examples include neutrophils, lymphocytes and monocytes.
White blood cells defend the body against disease-causing organisms.
Some engulf pathogens by phagocytosis, while lymphocytes produce antibodies.
written.followUp: Describe the main types of white blood cells and state their function.

rubric.why: White blood cells are colourless, nucleated blood cells.
rubric.description: States basic features of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that white blood cells are colourless and have a nucleus.

rubric.why: White blood cells are grouped into granulocytes and agranulocytes; examples include neutrophils, lymphocytes and monocytes.
rubric.description: Names the main groups or examples of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the two groups or at least two correct types.

rubric.why: White blood cells protect the body from infection through actions including phagocytosis and antibody production.
rubric.description: Explains the protective functions of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for stating their defence role and explaining a mechanism such as engulfing pathogens or producing antibodies.

written.text: Define endangered species. Give reasons of endangerment of the species found in Pakistan.
modelAnswer: An endangered species is a species whose population has fallen to such a low level that it is at risk of extinction.
In Pakistan, habitat destruction and deforestation reduce the food, shelter and breeding sites available to wildlife.
Illegal hunting and poaching directly reduce the populations of animals such as markhor and snow leopard.
Pollution and other human activities also damage habitats and threaten species, including aquatic wildlife such as the Indus dolphin.

rubric.why: An endangered species has a population so low that it is at risk of extinction.

rubric.description: Explains habitat destruction as a cause of endangerment.

rubric.why: Hunting, pollution and other human pressures can further reduce wildlife populations in Pakistan.
rubric.description: Gives other causes of endangerment.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for two further valid causes, or one cause explained clearly.

written.text: Write differences between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration requires oxygen; anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen.

Aerobic respiration completely breaks down glucose to carbon dioxide and water, whereas anaerobic respiration incompletely breaks it down, producing lactic acid in muscles or ethanol and carbon dioxide in yeast.
Aerobic respiration releases more energy than anaerobic respiration.
Aerobic respiration mainly occurs in the mitochondria, while anaerobic respiration takes place in the cytoplasm.

written.text: Write four benefits of electron microscope.
modelAnswer: An electron microscope provides much higher magnification than a light microscope.

It can be used to observe very small objects such as viruses.
It shows the fine structure of cells and their organelles.

rubric.description: States that an electron microscope provides higher magnification.

rubric.why: Its magnification and resolution allow fine cellular structures to be studied.

written.text: How is colonial organization unique from other organizations?
modelAnswer: A colonial organization is a group of similar cells living together.

written.text: What do you know about the term Species?
modelAnswer: A species is a group of similar organisms that can interbreed naturally.

written.text: Write down the Scientific Names of Mustard plant and Frog.

written.text: How does Lysosome work for the breakdown of food?
